rv.q: And it's beautiful: exquisitely written, performed and designed, with all of Birbiglia's characteristic ear for tone and rhythm.
Funny thing is, you never want him to shut up.
Birbiglia has become expert at finding the comedy in catastrophe, and the show builds to a climax that manages to be both hilarious and genuinely moving.
The latest Mike check-up, the funny and endearing The Old Man & the Pool, dives back into questions of life and death, delivered with a goofy gallows grin that helps the medicine go down.
In generously detailing the less-than-ideal fragments of his life, he reveals the many reasons we should keep relishing ours.
The Old Man & the Pool is one helluva sandwich.
Somehow, Birbiglia makes the business of death, the business of illness, the business of staying alive, the funniest thing.
In that respect, The Old Man and the Pool is Birbiglia at his most truthful.
Birbiglia has crafted a deeply personal and surprisingly moving meditation on mortality, middle age, and the small moments that define our lives.

Birbiglia's latest one-man show is a meditation on mortality, middle age, and the small moments that make life worth living, delivered with his trademark self-deprecating humor and masterful storytelling.
If you're a fan—or simply a fan of story-driven stand-up comedy—you should see Birbiglia live.
Here’s hoping that Birbiglia continues to come to Broadway each season with new autobiographical monologues and inspires the same kind of turnout.
When you’re in the good company of Birbiglia, after all, it feels perfectly normal to laugh in the face of death.
But it certainly demonstrates, if we needed any more proof, that at a Birbiglia show, it’s hard to stop laughing.

If you’re in the dumps, perhaps because you, too, have been contemplating life’s evanescence, I can think of no better way to cheer you up than a visit to Mike Birbiglia: The Old Man and the Pool, whose motto should be, “Come on in, the water’s fine.”
I was thoroughly enraptured by every word of a performance that flew by, and became the most fun I've had at a show in years, if not ever.
And if you ever thought about seeing a nutritionist, I challenge you to do so now with a straight face.
